## Correction from bug [rebar:941b-f049-5f29-4410] — this change's decision rule is REFUTED

Recording this here because 9790's own text is where the next reader will look, and its stated
rule is wrong in a way that is self-confirming.

9790's `not_ready_message` says: *'if it contains no `customfield_*` entries whatsoever the
plugin is still starting and the budget (JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT) is too short'*.

**Measured, experiment run 30981084637, against this exact image:**

    [before]            HTTP 200 total=27 customfield_count=0   EpicLink=False EpicName=False
    [after-180s-quiet]  HTTP 200 total=27 customfield_count=0   EpicLink=False EpicName=False
    create project -> HTTP 201
    [after-create+0s]   HTTP 200 total=55 customfield_count=13  EpicLink=True  EpicName=True

**GreenHopper provisions `Epic Link`/`Epic Name` when the first Jira Software PROJECT is
created, not when the plugin starts.** A 27-field, zero-`customfield_*` inventory is the
NORMAL state of a fresh instance with no project. It is not a plugin mid-start, and waiting
does not change it — 180 extra seconds of quiet moved nothing.

The consequence for this change: its session-start field wait was a **deadlock**, waiting for
something only the action it blocked could produce. It errored all 62 cells at fixture setup
(run 30975323866), and tripling the allowance to 1800s produced a byte-identical failure (run
30978613228). The 8m32s / 27-field observation 9790 cites from run 30944211742 is real — but
it is explained by 'no project existed', not by 'the plugin was still starting'.

The gate itself was a good idea in the wrong place: it is preserved and moved to
`_assert_project_capabilities`, which runs right after the project create — the first moment
the fields can exist. Gerrit change 1421.
